Subject: Reserved Slot Allocation — Week of Nov 6: ACME pilot ramp

Hi Graham / ACME procurement team,

Following up from yesterday's call — ACME's pilot is expected to jump from ~20 rps to ~120 rps for a short burst next week as you scale the integration tests. We've modeled the expected token mix in the attached ACME_weekly_capacity_table.xlsx and included an estimated reserved-slot ask: 4 x reserved slots (p4-equivalent) for the week of Nov 9-15 with a 20% buffer.

What we need to align on today so infra can lock capacity:
- Confirm PO timing / expected billing start date
- Whether you want committed monthly slots or a 7-day reserved tranche
- Any compliance or routing constraints (region/tenant isolation)

I've copied Finance (Laura) and Fleet Ops (Ben & Karthik) to confirm pricing and availability. Attachment: ACME_weekly_capacity_table.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Next steps: please reply with PO timing and whether the 7-day tranche is acceptable. If procurement prefers committed monthly pricing, Laura will run a quick delta analysis.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Reserved Slot Allocation — Week of Nov 6: ACME pilot ramp

Thanks Dylan — quick finance check.

Two items from our side:
1) Pricing model: A 7-day reserved tranche will be billed as a short-term commitment at 115% of the published hourly reserved rate (covers burst staffing). If ACME wants a monthly reserved commitment, the unit price improves ~18% but requires a 30-day minimum invoice period.
2) SLA / invoice alignment: we need to confirm start-of-billing vs start-of-usage. If ACME signs a PO with start-of-billing on Nov 9 but the integration causes use on Nov 8, we typically invoice from the first calendar day of chargeable usage.

I attached the SLA_terms_v3.pdf excerpt with the billing language we default to. If Procurement wants a carve-out on billing start, we can route through Marissa for an executive exception.

Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA_terms_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Graham Li <graham@acme.ai>, procure@acme.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved Slot Allocation — Week of Nov 6: ACME pilot ramp

Dylan / team,

We can provision 4 reserved P4-equivalent slots in us-west for the Nov 9-15 window. A few notes from Fleet Ops:
- We recommend explicit KV cache warming for any long-prefix workflows before the ramp — otherwise first-run latencies will spike. We can add a warm-up job; adds ~30 minutes of prep per slot.
- Buffer: we can keep a soft buffer of +1 slot (hot standby) for 6 hours each day; this is only charged if used.
- If ACME expects sustained >120 rps after the pilot, we should plan a monthly commitment (Laura's pricing) and start capacity reservations 10 business days prior to the billing start to avoid infra churn.

I'll hold the tentative capacity for 24 hours pending PO. Please confirm by EOD PST tomorrow and we'll lock the nodes.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Fleet Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: provisioning_checklist.md (text)
